sentences.text: Ms. Anita Kaithwas - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Vinod Tiwari - Panel Lawyer for State.
Heard on I.A. No.6445/2025, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant.
Appellant has been convicted under Sections 420 of IPC r/w Sections 366 and 376(2)(g) of IPC and sentenced to suffer R.I. for five years with fine of Rs.1000/- with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
Earlier, appellant was released on bail on 03.03.2005 but in the Covid-19 pandemic period, he could not contact his counsel, therefore, arrest warrant has been issued against him.
The Trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record.
The final disposal of this appeal would take considerable time.
Under such circumstances, application of appellant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail may be considered.
Learned counsel for State vehemently opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, I find it to be a fit case to suspend the jail sentence of appellant and to release her on bail, 2 CRA-293-2005 therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application of appellant is allowed.

Accordingly, I.A. No.6445/2025 stands allowed and it is directed that the jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and she be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court subject to verification of factum regarding deposit of fine amount.
Appellant is directed to appear before the trial Court first on 16.05.2025 and on other subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf.
Record of the trial Court be called for.
